questions: Q1: What CLI commands exist for library operations and what's missing?
Q2: What patterns should new commands follow?
Q3: What new CLI commands does finding #4 (manual reconcile in MVP) add?
Q4: How does finding #14 (acceptance test) affect the CLI?
Q5: Does finding #6 (optimistic concurrency) affect the iterate CLI command?

answers.answer: Current commands: list, show <ref>, comments list|post <ref>. Missing: create (new report from file), iterate <ref> --file (new version), publish <ref>, delete <ref>, reconcile (finding #4 — new for MVP). The publish and delete API endpoints already exist server-side (POST /library/items/:itemId/publish, DELETE /library/items/:itemId) but the CLI does not expose them. Create and iterate require new server endpoints.
evidence: src/library/index.ts: switch cases for list, show, comments only
Server api.ts lines 413-414: POST publish and DELETE endpoints exist
Ticket description: 'CLI (hlx library create --file, iterate <ref> --file, publish, delete)'

answers.answer: Consistent dispatcher pattern: subcommand router (index.ts) dispatches to command functions that call hxFetch with API key auth. Flag parsing via getFlag/requireFlag utilities. Reference resolution via resolve-library-item.ts (3-tier: exact ID, ticket short ID, title substring). New commands should follow this same structure. For file-based commands (create/iterate), the CLI would read local files and POST content to the API.
evidence: src/lib/http.ts: hxFetch with retry, API key auth, org header

answers.answer: Finding #4 moves manual reconcile from Round 2 to MVP. The CLI must add 'hlx library reconcile' as a new command that calls a server admin endpoint (e.g., POST /admin/library/reconcile). This command triggers a full scan of the library git repo to find unreconciled commits and create missing DB rows. It's the missed-webhook recovery valve.
evidence: report.html lines 1357-1359: 'Periodic reconciliation cron' was deferred to Round 2
Finding #4: 'Move a manual/cron reconcile into MVP (e.g. hlx library reconcile or an admin endpoint)'
hxFetch pattern at http.ts:37-134 supports basePath: '/api' for new endpoints

answers.answer: Finding #14 requires the feature to cleanly re-version RSH-667 and RSH-688 via 'hlx library iterate RSH-688 --file reports/RSH-688/report.html'. This is an explicit end-to-end acceptance criterion. The iterate command must support: (a) resolving a reference (ticket short ID) to a library item, (b) reading a local file, (c) calling the iterate API with the file content and baseCommitSha. This validates the entire authoring pipeline.
evidence: Finding #14: 'the feature must cleanly re-version RSH-667 and RSH-688 themselves via hlx library iterate --file'
resolve-library-item.ts:18-81: supports ticket short ID resolution

answers.answer: Yes. Finding #6 requires the iterate command to pass baseCommitSha to the server. The CLI must: (a) fetch the current item's latest version to get its commitSha, (b) pass that as baseCommitSha in the iterate request, (c) handle 409 Conflict responses with a clear error message ('Report has been updated since your last read. Please try again.').
evidence: Finding #6: 'require an expected baseCommitSha/version and reject stale writes'
No commitSha handling exists in any current CLI command

statement: The CLI needs five new commands: create, iterate, publish, delete, and reconcile (finding #4 — new MVP scope). Iterate must pass baseCommitSha for optimistic concurrency (finding #6). The acceptance test (finding #14) requires hlx library iterate --file to re-version RSH-667 and RSH-688. Publish and delete can use existing server endpoints. Create, iterate, and reconcile depend on new server API endpoints. All commands follow the established dispatcher + hxFetch + flag-parsing pattern.
